topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression by balancing constructive interference, reducing grating lobes, but increasing spillover loss. Tighter spacing enhances beamforming precision, while element tapering reduces sidelobes, optimizing capacity without compromising coverage.
reference_context: Ka-band satellites use spot beam coverage, allowing frequency reuse, and interleaved array spacing optimizes beamforming, reducing grating lobes and interference.
